correctness.rationale: Integrating U gives the sole positive lower-hit time x+√(x²+4μ) and s=−√(x²+4μ). On L, H(x)=x−x²/4 increases by 2μ; choosing the increasing branch x′<2 gives the stated analytic return. At a fixed point the two leg equations give p−s=μ and p+s=−4. Both hits are transverse for 0<μ<8 and each leg lasts μ. In X=x/2,z=μ/4 the exact multiplier is (z−1)(z+2)/[(z−2)(z+1)]; it has modulus below one for 0<z<√2, equals −1 at √2 and falls below −1 thereafter. Its z-derivative there is −4. The reproduced critical Taylor coefficients give B=T‴/6+(T″/2)²=9√2−12>0. For the second return, the displacement divided by the centered abscissa u is analytic and equals 2δ−2Bu²+O(δ²+|δu|+|u|³). This quotient is strictly concave in a fixed small neighborhood, with its unique local maximum at u=O(δ) of value 2δ+O(δ²), and negative at the two ends. Hence there are exactly two nearby nonzero roots for small positive δ and none for small negative δ. The two roots form one primitive cycle, with multiplier 1−4δ+O(δ^{3/2}); scaling x=2X recovers its physical amplitude, and continuity of the transverse flight times gives the period limit. At δ=0 the second return preserves each sign and strictly contracts |u| for small u≠0; successive even-return inverse squares differ by 4B+o(1). Summation, the unit magnitude of the odd-return multiplier, and x=2X give n(xₙ−p)²→2/B for the original return count. No statement beyond the transverse or local domain as specified is needed. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Replacing constant recovery with an affine vertical field is a simple, motivated next case in the threshold-relay model. It gives an explicit example of how recovery produces a transverse supercritical flip before tangency, with a sharp criterion and a calibrated relaxation rate in the physical section. The exact constants distinguish the dynamical regimes and quantify behavior that the general flip theorem alone does not predict. The contribution is local, not a global attractor classification.
